nodes.name: f-divergence scales with f
nodes.statement: For all $a \ge 0$, $D_{a f}(\mu, \nu) = a D_{f}(\mu, \nu)$.
assumptions: For all $a \ge 0$
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_mul

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Linearity of the integral.
nodes.statement_short: Linearity of the integral.

nodes.name: f-divergence is additive in f
nodes.statement:
$D_{f + g}(\mu, 
u) = D_f(\mu, 
u) + D_g(\mu, 
u)$.
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_add

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Linearity of the integral.
nodes.statement_short: Linearity of the integral.

nodes.name: Adding a linear term to f
nodes.statement:
For finite measures $\mu$ and $
u$ with $\mu(\mathcal X) = 
u(\mathcal X)$, for all $a \in \mathbb{R}$, $D_{f + a(x - 1)}(\mu, 
u) = D_{f}(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: For finite measures $\mu$ and $\nu$ with $\mu(\mathcal X) = \nu(\mathcal X)$
for all $a \in \mathbb{R}$
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_add_linear

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Linearity (Lemmas~\ref{lem:fDiv_add} and~\ref{lem:fDiv_mul}), then Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_const} and~\ref{lem:fDiv_id}.
nodes.statement_short: Linearity plus the constant and identity cases.

nodes.name: f-divergence invariant under measurable embeddings
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $g : \mathcal X 	o \mathcal Y$ be a measurable embedding. Then $D_f(g_* \mu, g_* 
u) = D_f(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $g : \mathcal X \to \mathcal Y$ be a measurable embedding.
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_map_measurableEmbedding

nodes.name: Symmetry of f-divergences via the perspective
nodes.statement: $D_f(\mu, \nu) = D_{x \mapsto xf(1/x)}(\nu, \mu)$~.
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_symm

nodes.name: f-divergence of a mixture in the first argument
nodes.statement:
For $a, b \ge 0$ with $a + b = 1$, $(\mu, 
u) \mapsto D_f(a \mu + b 
u, 
u)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto f(ax + b)$
assumptions: For $a, b \ge 0$ with $a + b = 1$
conclusions:
$(\mu, 
u) \mapsto D_f(a \mu + b 
u, 
u)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto f(ax + b)$
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_add_smul_left

nodes.name: f-divergence of a mixture in the second argument
nodes.statement: For $a, b \ge 0$ with $a + b = 1$, $(\mu, \nu) \mapsto D_f(\mu, a \mu + b \nu)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto (ax+b)f\left(\frac{x}{ax+b}\right)$~.
assumptions: For $a, b \ge 0$ with $a + b = 1$
conclusions: $(\mu, \nu) \mapsto D_f(\mu, a \mu + b \nu)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto (ax+b)f\left(\frac{x}{ax+b}\right)$
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_add_smul_right

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
We use Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_symm}, then Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_add_smul_left} and finally Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_symm} again:  egin{align*} D_f(\mu, a \mu + b 
u) &= D_{xf(1/x)}(a \mu + b 
u, \mu) \ &= D_{(bx+a)f(1/(bx+a))}(
u, \mu) \ &= D_{(ax+b)f(x/(ax+b))}(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Symmetry, the first-argument mixture lemma, then symmetry again.

nodes.name: f-divergence of a mixture in the second argument (variant)
nodes.statement:
For $a, b \ge 0$ with $a + b = 1$, $(\mu, 
u) \mapsto D_f(
u, a \mu + b 
u)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto (ax+b)f\left( rac{1}{ax+b}ight)$~.
assumptions: For $a, b \ge 0$ with $a + b = 1$
conclusions:
$(\mu, 
u) \mapsto D_f(
u, a \mu + b 
u)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto (ax+b)f\left( rac{1}{ax+b}ight)$
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_add_smul_right'

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
We use Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_add_smul_right}, then Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_symm}.  egin{align*} D_f(
u, a \mu + b 
u) &= D_{(bx+a)f\left( rac{x}{bx+a}ight)}(
u, \mu) = D_{(ax+b)f\left( rac{1}{ax+b}ight)}(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Second-argument mixture lemma followed by symmetry.

nodes.name: f-divergence with an added singular part
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu_1, \mu_2$ and $
u$ be finite measures on $\mathcal X$, with $\mu_1 \ll 
u$ and $\mu_2 \perp 
u$. Then $D_f(\mu_1 + \mu_2, 
u) = D_f(\mu_1, 
u) + \mu_2(\mathcal X) f'(\infty)$.
assumptions:
Let $\mu_1, \mu_2$ and $
u$ be finite measures on $\mathcal X$, with $\mu_1 \ll 
u$ and $\mu_2 \perp 
u$.
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_absolutelyContinuous_add_mutuallySingular

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
$ rac{d(\mu_1 + \mu_2)}{d 
u} =  rac{d \mu_1}{d 
u}$ a.e. and $(\mu_1 + \mu_2)_{\perp 
u} = \mu_2$.
nodes.statement_short: The density is unchanged and the singular part is $\mu_2$.

nodes.name: Subadditivity bound, absolutely continuous case
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu_1, \mu_2, 
u$ be three finite measures on $\mathcal X$ with $\mu_1 \ll 
u$ and $\mu_2 \ll 
u$. Then $D_f(\mu_1 + \mu_2, 
u) \le D_f(\mu_1, 
u) + \mu_2(\mathcal X) f'(\infty)$.
assumptions:
Let $\mu_1, \mu_2, 
u$ be three finite measures on $\mathcal X$ with $\mu_1 \ll 
u$ and $\mu_2 \ll 
u$.
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_add_measure_le_of_ac

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
egin{align*} D_f(\mu_1 + \mu_2, 
u) &= \int_x f \left(  rac{d \mu_1}{d
u}(x) +  rac{d\mu_2}{d
u}(x) ight) \partial 
u \ &\le \int_x f \left(  rac{d \mu_1}{d
u}(x) ight) +  rac{d\mu_2}{d
u}(x) f'(\infty) \partial 
u \ &= D_f(\mu_1, 
u) + \mu_2(\mathcal X) f'(\infty) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Pointwise bound $f(a+b) \le f(a) + b f'(\infty)$ from convexity, then integrate.

nodes.name: Subadditivity bound for adding a measure
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu_1, \mu_2, 
u$ be three finite measures on $\mathcal X$. Then $D_f(\mu_1 + \mu_2, 
u) \le D_f(\mu_1, 
u) + \mu_2(\mathcal X) f'(\infty)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu_1, \mu_2, \nu$ be three finite measures on $\mathcal X$.
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_add_measure_le

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
From Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_absolutelyContinuous_add_mutuallySingular}, then Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_add_measure_le_of_ac},  egin{align*} D_f(\mu_1 + \mu_2, 
u) &= D_f( rac{d\mu_1}{d 
u}\cdot 
u +  rac{d\mu_2}{d 
u}\cdot 
u, 
u) + (\mu_1)_{\perp
u}(\mathcal X) f'(\infty) + (\mu_2)_{\perp
u}(\mathcal X) f'(\infty) \ &\le D_f( rac{d\mu_1}{d 
u}\cdot 
u, 
u) + ( rac{d\mu_2}{d 
u}\cdot 
u)(\mathcal X) f'(\infty) + (\mu_1)_{\perp
u}(\mathcal X) f'(\infty) + (\mu_2)_{\perp
u}(\mathcal X) f'(\infty) \ &= D_f(\mu_1, 
u) + \mu_2(\mathcal X) f'(\infty) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Split into absolutely continuous and singular parts, then apply the absolutely continuous case.

nodes.name: f-divergence decomposition into absolutely continuous and singular parts
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$. Then $D_f(\mu, 
u) = D_f( rac{d\mu}{d
u}\cdot 
u, 
u) + f'(\infty) \mu_{\perp 
u}(\mathcal X)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$.
nodes.label: lem:fDiv_eq_add_withDensity_derivAtTop

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
Apply Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_absolutelyContinuous_add_mutuallySingular} to $ rac{d\mu}{d
u}\cdot 
u$ and $\mu_{\perp 
u}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the singular-part lemma to the Lebesgue decomposition of $\mu$.

nodes.name: Jensen lower bound, absolutely continuous case
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on the same space $\mathcal X$, such that $\mu \ll 
u$. Then $
u(\mathcal X) f(\mu(\mathcal X)/
u(\mathcal X)) \le D_f(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on the same space $\mathcal X$, such that $\mu \ll \nu$.
conclusions:
Then $
u(\mathcal X) f(\mu(\mathcal X)/
u(\mathcal X)) \le D_f(\mu, 
u)$.
nodes.label: lem:le_fDiv_of_ac

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement_short: Jensen's inequality for the normalized measure $\nu/\nu(\mathcal X)$.

nodes.name: Only the integral part remains
nodes.statement: Since $\mu \ll \nu$ the $f$-divergence is only the integral part.
nodes.statement_short: Only the integral part remains.

nodes.name: Trivial case $\nu = 0$
nodes.statement: If $\nu = 0$ there is nothing to prove.
nodes.statement_short: Trivial case $\nu = 0$.

nodes.name: Apply Jensen's inequality for the normalized measure
nodes.statement_short: Apply Jensen's inequality for the normalized measure.

nodes.name: Jensen lower bound for f-divergences
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on the same space $\mathcal X$. Then $
u(\mathcal X) f(\mu(\mathcal X)/
u(\mathcal X)) \le D_f(\mu, 
u)$. In particular, if $
u$ is a probability measure, $f(\mu(\mathcal X)) \le D_f(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on the same space $\mathcal X$.
conclusions:
Then $
u(\mathcal X) f(\mu(\mathcal X)/
u(\mathcal X)) \le D_f(\mu, 
u)$.
In particular, if $\nu$ is a probability measure, $f(\mu(\mathcal X)) \le D_f(\mu, \nu)$.
nodes.label: lem:le_fDiv

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:

u(\mathcal X) f( rac{d\mu}{d
u}\cdot
