nodes.statement_short: Second Bretagnolle-Huber bound with the Hellinger function, dropping a nonnegative term.

nodes.name: Statistical information is an f-divergence
nodes.statement: On probability measures, the statistical information $\mathcal I_\xi$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $\phi_{\xi_0, \xi_1}$ of Definition~\ref{def:statInfoFun}.
conclusions: On probability measures, the statistical information $\mathcal I_\xi$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $\phi_{\xi_0, \xi_1}$ of Definition~\ref{def:statInfoFun}
nodes.label: lem:statInfo_eq_fDiv

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is a reformulation of Theorem~\ref{thm:statInfo_eq_integral}.
nodes.statement_short: Reformulation of the integral form of the statistical information.

nodes.name: TV is an f-divergence
nodes.statement: On probability measures, the total variation distance $\TV$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto \frac{1}{2}\vert x - 1 \vert$.
conclusions: On probability measures, the total variation distance $\TV$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto \frac{1}{2}\vert x - 1 \vert$
nodes.label: lem:tv_eq_fDiv

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is a reformulation of Lemma~\ref{lem:tv_eq_integral_abs}.
nodes.statement_short: Reformulation of the integral form of TV.

nodes.name: Kullback-Leibler divergence
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$. The Kullback-Leibler divergence between $\mu$ and $
u$ is  egin{align*} \KL(\mu, 
u) = \mu\left[\log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}ight] \end{align*} if $\mu \ll 
u$ and $x \mapsto \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is $\mu$-integrable and $+\infty$ otherwise.
nodes.label: def:KL

nodes.name: KL is an f-divergence
nodes.statement: $\KL(\mu, \nu) = D_f(\mu, \nu)$ for $f: x \mapsto x \log x$.
nodes.label: lem:kl_eq_fDiv

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Simple computation.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation.

nodes.name: Conditional Kullback-Leibler divergence
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be two kernels. The conditional Kullback-Leibler divergence between $\kappa$ and $\eta$ with respect to $\mu$ is \begin{align*} \KL(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu) = \mu\left[x \mapsto \KL(\kappa(x), \eta(x))\right] \end{align*} if $x \mapsto \KL(\kappa(x), \eta(x))$ is $\mu$-integrable and $+\infty$ otherwise.
nodes.label: def:condKL

nodes.name: Conditional KL is a conditional f-divergence
nodes.statement: $\KL(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu) = D_f(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu)$ for $f: x \mapsto x \log x$.
nodes.label: lem:condKL_eq_condFDiv

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Simple computation.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation.

nodes.name: KL of a measure with itself
nodes.label: lem:kl_self

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: KL is an f-divergence thanks to Lemma~\ref{lem:kl_eq_fDiv}, then apply Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_self}.
nodes.statement_short: KL is an f-divergence; apply the self-divergence lemma.

nodes.name: Conditional KL of constant kernels
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be finite measures on $\mathcal X$, $\xi$ be a finite measure on $\mathcal Y$. Then $\KL(x \mapsto \mu, x \mapsto 
u \mid \xi) = \KL(\mu, 
u) \xi (\mathcal X)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be finite measures on $\mathcal X$, $\xi$ be a finite measure on $\mathcal Y$.
nodes.label: lem:condKL_const

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: KL is an f-divergence thanks to Lemma~\ref{lem:kl_eq_fDiv} and Lemma~\ref{lem:condKL_eq_condFDiv}, then apply Lemma~\ref{lem:condFDiv_const}.
nodes.statement_short: KL as an f-divergence; apply the constant-kernel lemma.

nodes.name: Marginals for KL
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be two measures on $\mathcal X 	imes \mathcal Y$, and let $\mu_X, 
u_X$ be their marginals on $\mathcal X$. Then $\KL(\mu_X, 
u_X) \le \KL(\mu, 
u)$. Similarly, for $\mu_Y, 
u_Y$ the marginals on $\mathcal Y$, $\KL(\mu_Y, 
u_Y) \le \KL(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu$ and $\nu$ be two measures on $\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y$, and let $\mu_X, \nu_X$ be their marginals on $\mathcal X$.
conclusions:
Similarly, for $\mu_Y, 
u_Y$ the marginals on $\mathcal Y$, $\KL(\mu_Y, 
u_Y) \le \KL(\mu, 
u)$.
nodes.label: thm:kl_fst_le

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:fDiv_fst_le_2}.
nodes.statement_short: Special case of the marginal inequality for f-divergences.

nodes.name: Data-processing inequality for KL
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\kappa : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be a Markov kernel. Then $\KL(\kappa \circ \mu, \kappa \circ 
u) \le \KL(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be a Markov kernel.
nodes.label: thm:kl_data_proc

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:fDiv_data_proc_2}.
nodes.statement_short: Special case of the DPI for f-divergences.

nodes.name: KL lower bound by masses
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$. Then $\KL(\mu, 
u) \ge \mu(\mathcal X) \log  rac{\mu(\mathcal X)}{
u(\mathcal X)}$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$.
nodes.label: lem:kl_ge

nodes.name: Gibbs' inequality
nodes.statement: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures. Then $\KL(\mu, \nu) \ge 0$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures.
nodes.label: lem:kl_nonneg

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:kl_ge} and use $\mu(\mathcal X) = \nu (\mathcal X)$.
nodes.statement_short: Mass lower bound with equal masses.

nodes.name: Converse Gibbs' inequality
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures. Then $\KL(\mu, 
u) = 0$ if and only if $\mu = 
u$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures.
nodes.label: lem:kl_eq_zero_iff

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: KL is an f-divergence thanks to Lemma~\ref{lem:kl_eq_fDiv}, then apply Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_eq_zero_iff}.
nodes.statement_short: KL as an f-divergence with strictly convex $x\log x$.

nodes.name: Convexity of KL
nodes.statement: $(\mu, \nu) \mapsto \KL(\mu, \nu)$ is convex.
nodes.label: lem:kl_convex

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:fDiv_convex}
nodes.statement_short: Special case of joint convexity of f-divergences.

nodes.name: Integrability of the log-likelihood ratio of composition-products
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be two Markov kernels such that $\mu \otimes \kappa \ll 
u \otimes \eta$. Then $p \mapsto \log  rac{d \mu \otimes \kappa}{d 
u \otimes \eta}(p)$ is $\mu \otimes \kappa$-integrable if and only if the following hold:  egin{enumerate} \item $x \mapsto \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is $\mu$-integrable \item $x \mapsto \int_y \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \kappa(x)$ is $\mu$-integrable \item for $\mu$-almost all $x$, $y \mapsto \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\kappa(x)$-integrable \end{enumerate}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be two Markov kernels such that $\mu \otimes \kappa \ll \nu \otimes \eta$.
conclusions: Then $p \mapsto \log \frac{d \mu \otimes \kappa}{d \nu \otimes \eta}(p)$ is $\mu \otimes \kappa$-integrable if and only if the following hold: \begin{enumerate} \item $x \mapsto \log \frac{d \mu}{d \nu}(x)$ is $\mu$-integrable \item $x \mapsto \int_y \log \frac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \kappa(x)$ is $\mu$-integrable \item for $\mu$-almost all $x$, $y \mapsto \log \frac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\kappa(x)$-integrable \end{enumerate}
nodes.label: lem:integrable_llr_compProd_iff

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
Note that from the hypothesis it easily follows that $\mu \ll 
u$ and $\mu$-a.e.\ $\kappa(x) \ll \eta(x)$. Applying Lemma~ef{lem:integrable_fDiv_compProd_iff} we know that $\log  rac{d \mu \otimes \kappa}{d 
u \otimes \eta}$ is $
u \otimes \eta$-integrable iff the following hold:  egin{enumerate} \item[i.] for $
u$-almost all $x$, $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) $ is $\eta(x)$-integrable \item[ii.] $x \mapsto \int_y  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \eta (x)$ is $
u$-integrable \end{enumerate} { fseries(i.$\Leftarrow$)} 3.\ implies that $
u$-a.e.\ $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\kappa(x)$-integrable, hence $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable $
u$-a.e.\ Moreover $y \mapsto  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable, then, since $ rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is constant in $y$, $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable. This allows us to conclude that $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) +  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) =  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable $
u$-a.e. { fseries(ii.$\Leftarrow$)} 1.\ implies that $x \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is $
u$-integrable. 2.\ implies that $x \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \int_y  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \eta(x)$ is $
u$-integrable. Therefore $$x \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) +  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \int_y  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \eta(x) = \int_y  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \eta (x)$$ is $
u$-integrable. { fseries($\Rightarrow$1.)} This follows from the hypothesis applying a more general Lemma for f divergences, see ProbabilityTheory.integrable\_f\_rnDeriv\_of\_integrable\_compProd' in the lean code. { fseries($\Rightarrow$3.)} i.\ implies that $\mu$-a.e.\ $y \mapsto  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable, hence $y \mapsto \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) = \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) + \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\kappa(x)$-integrable. Then, since $\log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is constant in $y$ and $\kappa(x)$ is a finite measure, $y \mapsto \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\kappa(x)$-integrable. { fseries($\Rightarrow$2.)} ii.\ implies that $x \mapsto \int_y  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \eta (x) = \int_y \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \kappa (x)$ is $\mu$-integrable. Thanks to 3.\ we can split the integral: $$\int_y \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \kappa (x) = \int_y \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \partial \kappa (x) + \int_y \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \kappa (x) = \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) + \int_y \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \kappa (x)$$ Then using 1.\ we can conclude that $x \mapsto \int_y \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \kappa (x)$ is $\mu$-integrable.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce via the f-divergence integrability lemma to two conditions and check each implication between them and items 1-3.

nodes.name: Absolute continuity of the components; reduce to conditions i. and ii
nodes.statement:
Note that from the hypothesis it easily follows that $\mu \ll 
u$ and $\mu$-a.e.\ $\kappa(x) \ll \eta(x)$. Applying Lemma~ef{lem:integrable_fDiv_compProd_iff} we know that $\log  rac{d \mu \otimes \kappa}{d 
u \otimes \eta}$ is $
u \otimes \eta$-integrable iff the following hold:  egin{enumerate} \item[i.] for $
u$-almost all $x$, $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) $ is $\eta(x)$-integrable \item[ii.] $x \mapsto \int_y  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \eta (x)$ is $
u$-integrable \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Absolute continuity of the components; reduce to conditions i. and ii.

nodes.name: Condition i
nodes.statement:
[i.] for $
u$-almost all $x$, $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) $ is $\eta(x)$-integrable
nodes.statement_short: Condition i.

nodes.name: Condition ii
nodes.statement:
[ii.] $x \mapsto \int_y  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \eta (x)$ is $
u$-integrable \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Condition ii.

nodes.name: Items 1-3 imply condition i
nodes.statement:
{ fseries(i.$\Leftarrow$)} 3.\ implies that $
u$-a.e.\ $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\kappa(x)$-integrable, hence $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable $
u$-a.e.\ Moreover $y \mapsto  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable, then, since $ rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is constant in $y$, $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable. This allows us to conclude that $y \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) +  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) =  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable $
u$-a.e.
nodes.statement_short: Items 1-3 imply condition i.

nodes.name: Items 1-3 imply condition ii
nodes.statement:
{ fseries(ii.$\Leftarrow$)} 1.\ implies that $x \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is $
u$-integrable. 2.\ implies that $x \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \int_y  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \eta(x)$ is $
u$-integrable. Therefore $$x \mapsto  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) +  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \int_y  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \eta(x) = \int_y  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \eta (x)$$ is $
u$-integrable.
nodes.statement_short: Items 1-3 imply condition ii.

nodes.name: Integrability gives item 1
nodes.statement: {\bfseries($\Rightarrow$1.)} This follows from the hypothesis applying a more general Lemma for f divergences, see ProbabilityTheory.integrable\_f\_rnDeriv\_of\_integrable\_compProd' in the lean code.
nodes.statement_short: Integrability gives item 1.

nodes.name: Condition i. gives item 3
nodes.statement:
{ fseries($\Rightarrow$3.)} i.\ implies that $\mu$-a.e.\ $y \mapsto  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight)$ is $\eta(x)$-integrable, hence $y \mapsto \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) = \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) + \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\kappa(x)$-integrable. Then, since $\log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)$ is constant in $y$ and $\kappa(x)$ is a finite measure, $y \mapsto \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)$ is $\kappa(x)$-integrable.
nodes.statement_short: Condition i. gives item 3.

nodes.name: Condition ii. and item 3 give item 2
nodes.statement:
{ fseries($\Rightarrow$2.)} ii.\ implies that $x \mapsto \int_y  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \eta (x) = \int_y \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \kappa (x)$ is $\mu$-integrable. Thanks to 3.\ we can split the integral: $$\int_y \log \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) ight) \partial \kappa (x) = \int_y \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) \partial \kappa (x) + \int_y \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \kappa (x) = \log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) + \int_y \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \kappa (x)$$ Then using 1.\ we can conclude that $x \mapsto \int_y \log  rac{d \kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y) \partial \kappa (x)$ is $\mu$-integrable.
nodes.statement_short: Condition ii. and item 3 give item 2.

nodes.name: Chain rule for KL with composition-product second term
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ two Markov kernels. Then $\KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, 
u \otimes \eta) = \KL(\mu, 
u) + \KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, \mu \otimes \eta)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ two Markov kernels.
nodes.label: thm:kl_compProd_aux

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~ef{lem:ac_compProd_iff}, $\mu \otimes \kappa \ll 
u \otimes \eta \iff \left( \mu \ll 
u \ \wedge \ \mu \otimes \kappa \ll \mu \otimes \eta ight)$. Hence if any of the two sides of the equality is infinite due to a lack of absolute continuity, the other is as well. We now suppose that $\mu \otimes \kappa \ll 
u \otimes \eta$, $\mu \ll 
u$ and $\mu \otimes \kappa \ll \mu \otimes \eta$. TODO: deal with the non-integrable case, without using Lemma~ef{lem:integrable_llr_compProd_iff} that requires countably generated sigma-algebras. Suppose then that all three log-likelihood ratios are integrable. We use the chain rule for Radon-Nikodym derivatives (Theorem~ef{thm:rnDeriv_chain_compProd}).  egin{align*} \KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, 
u \otimes \eta) &= \int_p \log  rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d(
u \otimes \eta)}(p) \partial (\mu \otimes \kappa) \ &= \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x) rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d (\mu \otimes \eta)}(x,y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x)ight) + \log \left( rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d (\mu \otimes \eta)}(x,y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \int_x \log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)\partial\mu + \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d (\mu \otimes \eta)}(x,y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \int_x \log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)\partial\mu + \int_p\log \left( rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d (\mu \otimes \eta)}(p)ight) \partial (\mu \otimes \kappa) \ &= \KL(\mu, 
u) + \KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, \mu \otimes \eta) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Absolute-continuity case analysis, then the chain rule for Radon-Nikodym derivatives and splitting the logarithm.

nodes.name: Both sides are infinite together when absolute continuity fails
nodes.statement: By Lemma~\ref{lem:ac_compProd_iff}, $\mu \otimes \kappa \ll \nu \otimes \eta \iff \left( \mu \ll \nu \ \wedge \ \mu \otimes \kappa \ll \mu \otimes \eta \right)$. Hence if any of the two sides of the equality is infinite due to a lack of absolute continuity, the other is as well.
nodes.statement_short: Both sides are infinite together when absolute continuity fails.

nodes.name: Assume absolute continuity and integrability
nodes.statement: We now suppose that $\mu \otimes \kappa \ll \nu \otimes \eta$, $\mu \ll \nu$ and $\mu \otimes \kappa \ll \mu \otimes \eta$. TODO: deal with the non-integrable case, without using Lemma~\ref{lem:integrable_llr_compProd_iff} that requires countably generated sigma-algebras. Suppose then that all three log-likelihood ratios are integrable.
nodes.statement_short: Assume absolute continuity and integrability.

nodes.name: Chain rule for densities and split the log
nodes.statement:
We use the chain rule for Radon-Nikodym derivatives (Theorem~ef{thm:rnDeriv_chain_compProd}).  egin{align*} \KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, 
u \otimes \eta) &= \int_p \log  rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d(
u \otimes \eta)}(p) \partial (\mu \otimes \kappa) \ &= \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x) rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d (\mu \otimes \eta)}(x,y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x)ight) + \log \left( rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d (\mu \otimes \eta)}(x,y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \int_x \log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)\partial\mu + \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d (\mu \otimes \eta)}(x,y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \int_x \log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)\partial\mu + \int_p\log \left( rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d (\mu \otimes \eta)}(p)ight) \partial (\mu \otimes \kappa) \ &= \KL(\mu, 
u) + \KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, \mu \otimes \eta) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Chain rule for densities and split the log.

nodes.name: Chain rule for KL, kernel version
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ two Markov kernels, with either $\mathcal X$ countable or $\mathcal{Y}$ countably generated. Then $\KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, 
u \otimes \eta) = \KL(\mu, 
u) + \KL(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ two Markov kernels, with either $\mathcal X$ countable or $\mathcal{Y}$ countably generated.
nodes.label: thm:kl_compProd

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
Handle the case where $\mu \otimes \kappa$ is not absolutely continuous with respect to $
u \otimes \eta$ first, then the case where $p \mapsto \log  rac{d \mu \otimes \kappa}{d 
u \otimes \eta}(p)$ is not $\mu \otimes \kappa$-integrable using Lemma~ef{lem:integrable_llr_compProd_iff}. For the case where $\mu \otimes \kappa \ll 
u \otimes \eta$ and $p \mapsto \log  rac{d \mu \otimes \kappa}{d 
u \otimes \eta}(p)$ is $\mu \otimes \kappa$-integrable use Lemma~ef{lem:rnDeriv_compProd} and Corollary~ef{cor:rnDeriv_value} in a computation:  egin{align*} \KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, 
u \otimes \eta) &= \int_p \log  rac{d(\mu \otimes \kappa)}{d(
u \otimes \eta)}(p) \partial (\mu \otimes \kappa) \ &= \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x) rac{d\kappa}{d \eta}(x,y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x)ight) + \log \left( rac{d\kappa}{d \eta}(x,y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \int_x \log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)\partial\mu + \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d\kappa}{d \eta}(x,y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \int_x \log \left( rac{d\mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)\partial\mu + \int_x \int_y\log \left( rac{d\kappa(x)}{d \eta(x)}(y)ight) \partial \kappa(x) \partial\mu \ &= \KL(\mu, 
u) + \KL(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Handle non-absolutely-continuous and non-integrable cases, then compute with the kernel Radon-Nikodym derivative.

nodes.name: Chain rule for KL, with Bayesian inverse
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ two Markov kernels with Bayesian inverses $\kappa_\mu^\dagger$ and $\eta_
u^\dagger$. Then  egin{align*} \KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, 
u \otimes \eta) = \KL(\kappa \circ \mu, \eta \circ 
u) + \KL(\kappa_\mu^\dagger, \eta_
u^\dagger \mid \kappa \circ \mu) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ two Markov kernels with Bayesian inverses $\kappa_\mu^\dagger$ and $\eta_\nu^\dagger$.
nodes.label: thm:kl_compProd_bayesInv

nodes.name: Chain rule for KL, product version
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X 	imes \mathcal Y$, where $\mathcal Y$ is standard Borel. Then $\KL(\mu, 
u) = \KL(\mu_X, 
u_X) + \KL(\mu_{Y|X}, 
u_{Y|X} \mid \mu_X)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y$, where $\mathcal Y$ is standard Borel.
nodes.label: thm:kl_fst_add_condKL

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
Write $\mu = \mu_X \otimes \mu_{Y|X}$ and $
u = 
u_X \otimes 
u_{Y|X}$, then use Theorem~ef{thm:kl_compProd}.
nodes.statement_short: Disintegrate both measures and apply the kernel chain rule.

nodes.name: KL of products with finite first factors
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu_1, 
u_1$ be finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\mu_2, 
u_2$ probability measures on $\mathcal{Y}$. Then $$\KL(\mu_1	imes \mu_2, 
u_1 	imes 
u_2) = \KL(\mu_1, 
u_1) + \KL(\mu_2, 
u_2) \mu_1 (\mathcal X) \: .$$
assumptions: Let $\mu_1, \nu_1$ be finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\mu_2, \nu_2$ probability measures on $\mathcal{Y}$.
nodes.label: lem:kl_prod_two'

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Write $\mu_1 \times \mu_2$ and $\nu_1 \times \nu_2$ as composition products of a measure and a constant kernel, then apply the chain rule (Theorem~\ref{thm:kl_compProd}) and Lemma~\ref{lem:condKL_const}.
nodes.statement_short: Products as composition-products with constant kernels; chain rule and the constant-kernel lemma.

nodes.name: Tensorization of KL
nodes.statement:
For $\mu_1$ a probability measure on $\mathcal X$, $
u_1$ a finite measure on $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mu_2, 
u_2$ two probability measures on $\mathcal Y$,  egin{align*} \KL(\mu_1 	imes \mu_2, 
u_1 	imes 
u_2) = \KL(\mu_1, 
u_1) + \KL(\mu_2 	imes 
u_2) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\mu_1$ a probability measure on $\mathcal X$, $\nu_1$ a finite measure on $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mu_2, \nu_2$ two probability measures on $\mathcal Y$
nodes.label: thm:kl_prod_two

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is a particular case of Lemma~\ref{lem:kl_prod_two'}.
nodes.statement_short: Special case of the product formula.

nodes.name: Tensorization of KL, finite product
assumptions: Let $I$ be a finite index set.
Let $(\mu_i)_{i \in I}, (\nu_i)_{i \in I}$ be probability measures on spaces $(\mathcal X_i)_{i \in I}$.
nodes.label: thm:kl_pi

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Induction on the size of $I$, using Theorem~\ref{thm:kl_prod_two}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $|I|$ using two-factor tensorization.

nodes.name: KL chain rule conditioned on an event
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two measures and $E$ an event. Let $\mu_{|E}$ be the measure defined by $\mu_{|E}(A) =  rac{\mu(A \cap E)}{\mu(E)}$ and define $
u_{|E}$, $\mu_{| E^c}$ and $
u_{| E^c}$ similarly. Let $\kl(p,q) = p\log rac{p}{q} + (1-p)\log rac{1-p}{1-q}$ be the Kullback-Leibler divergence between Bernoulli distributions with means $p$ and $q$. Then  egin{align*} \KL(\mu, 
u) \ge \kl(\mu(E), 
u(E)) + \mu(E) \KL(\mu_{|E}, 
u_{|E}) + \mu(E^c) \KL(\mu_{|E^c}, 
u_{|E^c}) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two measures and $E$ an event.
Let $\mu_{|E}$ be the measure defined by $\mu_{|E}(A) = \frac{\mu(A \cap E)}{\mu(E)}$ and define $\nu_{|E}$, $\mu_{| E^c}$ and $\nu_{| E^c}$ similarly.
Let $\kl(p,q) = p\log\frac{p}{q} + (1-p)\log\frac{1-p}{1-q}$ be the Kullback-Leibler divergence between Bernoulli distributions with means $p$ and $q$.
nodes.label: lem:kl_chain_rule_cond_event

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu_E$ be the Bernoulli distribution with $\mu_E(\{1\}) = \mu(E)$, and define $
u_E$ similarly. Let $\kappa : \{0,1\} ightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel defined by $\kappa(1) = \mu_{|E}$ and $\kappa(0) = \mu_{|E^c}$. Define a kernel $\eta$ similarly for $
u$. Then $\mu = \kappa \circ \mu_E$ and $
u = \eta \circ 
u_E$. $\mu_E \otimes \kappa$ is equal to the composition of $\mu$ and the deterministic kernel given by the function $f : x \mapsto (\mathbb{I}_E(x), x)$. By Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_compProd_prod_eq}, that gives $\KL(\mu_E \otimes \kappa, 
u_E \otimes \eta) = \KL(\mu, 
u)$. Using the chain rule (Theorem~ef{thm:kl_compProd}),  egin{align*} \KL(\mu_E \otimes \kappa, 
u_E \otimes \eta) &= \KL(\mu_E, 
u_E) + \KL(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu_E) \ &= \KL(\mu_E, 
u_E) + \mu(E) \KL(\mu_{|E}, 
u_{|E}) + \mu(E^c) \KL(\mu_{|E^c}, 
u_{|E^c}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Write $\mu$ as a mixture over the indicator of $E$, use invariance under the graph kernel and the KL chain rule.

nodes.name: Write $\mu,\nu$ as compositions of Bernoulli laws with conditional kernels
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu_E$ be the Bernoulli distribution with $\mu_E(\{1\}) = \mu(E)$, and define $
u_E$ similarly. Let $\kappa : \{0,1\} ightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel defined by $\kappa(1) = \mu_{|E}$ and $\kappa(0) = \mu_{|E^c}$. Define a kernel $\eta$ similarly for $
u$. Then $\mu = \kappa \circ \mu_E$ and $
u = \eta \circ 
u_E$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $\mu,\nu$ as compositions of Bernoulli laws with conditional kernels.

nodes.name: The joint law has the same KL as $(\mu,\nu)$
nodes.statement: $\mu_E \otimes \kappa$ is equal to the composition of $\mu$ and the deterministic kernel given by the function $f : x \mapsto (\mathbb{I}_E(x), x)$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_compProd_prod_eq}, that gives $\KL(\mu_E \otimes \kappa, \nu_E \otimes \eta) = \KL(\mu, \nu)$.
nodes.statement_short: The joint law has the same KL as $(\mu,\nu)$.

nodes.name: Apply the chain rule
nodes.statement:
Using the chain rule (Theorem~ef{thm:kl_compProd}),  egin{align*} \KL(\mu_E \otimes \kappa, 
u_E \otimes \eta) &= \KL(\mu_E, 
u_E) + \KL(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu_E) \ &= \KL(\mu_E, 
u_E) + \mu(E) \KL(\mu_{|E}, 
u_{|E}) + \mu(E^c) \KL(\mu_{|E^c}, 
u_{|E^c}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the chain rule.

nodes.name: Expected log-likelihood ratio on an event
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two measures and $E$ an event. Then $\mu(E)\log rac{\mu(E)}{
u(E)} \le \mu\left[\mathbb{I}(E)\log  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}ight]$ .
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two measures and $E$ an event.
nodes.label: lem:expectation_llr_event

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:kl_ge} to the measures $\mu$ and $\nu$ restricted to $E$. $\mu\left[\mathbb{I}(E)\log \frac{d \mu}{d \nu}\right]$ is the KL between those two distributions.
nodes.statement_short: Mass lower bound for KL applied to the restrictions to $E$.

nodes.name: Hellinger alpha-divergence
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$. The Hellinger divergence of order $\alpha \in [0,+\infty)$ between $\mu$ and $
u$ is  egin{align*} \He_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \left\{  egin{array}{ll} 
u \{x \mid  rac{d\mu}{d
u} (x) = 0\} & 	ext{for } \alpha = 0 \ \KL(\mu, 
u) & 	ext{for } \alpha = 1 \ D_{f_\alpha}(\mu, 
u) & 	ext{for } \alpha \in (0,+\infty)  ackslash \{1\} \end{array}ight. \end{align*} with $f_\alpha : x \mapsto  rac{x^{\alpha} - 1}{\alpha - 1}$.
nodes.label: def:hellingerAlpha

nodes.name: Hellinger divergence of order below 1 is finite
nodes.statement: For $\alpha \in [0, 1)$ and finite measures $\mu, \nu$, $\He_\alpha(\mu, \nu) < \infty$.
assumptions: For $\alpha \in [0, 1)$ and finite measures $\mu, \nu$
nodes.label: lem:hellingerAlpha_ne_top_of_lt_one

nodes.name: Integral formula for Hellinger divergences
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha \in (0,1)\cup(1, \infty)$, $\mu$ a finite measure and $
u$ a probability measure, if $\He_\alpha(\mu, 
u) < \infty$ then  egin{align*} \He_\alpha(\mu, 
u) =  rac{1}{\alpha - 1} \left( \int_x \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)^\alpha \partial 
u - 1 ight) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\alpha \in (0,1)\cup(1, \infty)$, $\mu$ a finite measure and $\nu$ a probability measure
if $\He_\alpha(\mu, \nu) < \infty$
nodes.label: lem:hellingerAlpha_eq_integral

nodes.name: Symmetry of the integral of powers of the density
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha \in (0,1)\cup(1, \infty)$, $\mu, 
u$ two sigma-finite measures,  egin{align*} \int_x \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)^\alpha \partial 
u = \int_x \left( rac{d 
u}{d \mu}(x)ight)^{1 - \alpha} \partial \mu \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\alpha \in (0,1)\cup(1, \infty)$, $\mu, \nu$ two sigma-finite measures
nodes.label: lem:integral_rpow_rnDeriv_symm

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
egin{align*} \int_x \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)^\alpha \partial 
u &= \int_x \left( rac{d \mu}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x) \left( rac{d 
u}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x)ight)^{-1} ight)^\alpha \partial 
u \ &= \int_x \left( rac{d \mu}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x) \left( rac{d 
u}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x)ight)^{-1} ight)^\alpha  rac{d 
u}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x) \partial (\mu + 
u) \ &= \int_x \left( rac{d \mu}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x) \left( rac{d 
u}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x)ight)^{-1} ight)^{\alpha - 1}  rac{d \mu}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x) \partial (\mu + 
u) \ &= \int_x \left( rac{d \mu}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x) \left( rac{d 
u}{d (\mu + 
u)}(x)ight)^{-1} ight)^{\alpha - 1} \partial \mu \ &= \int_x \left( rac{d 
u}{d \mu}(x)ight)^{1 - \alpha} \partial \mu \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Change the dominating measure to $\mu+\nu$ and back.

nodes.name: Skew symmetry of Hellinger divergences
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and finite measures $\mu, 
u$, $(1 - \alpha) \He_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \alpha \He_{1 - \alpha}(
u, \mu)$.
assumptions: For $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and finite measures $\mu, \nu$
nodes.label: lem:hellingerAlpha_symm

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Use Lemma~\ref{lem:integral_rpow_rnDeriv_symm}.
nodes.statement_short: From the symmetry of the integral of density powers.

nodes.name: Conditional Hellinger alpha-divergence
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be two kernels. The conditional Hellinger divergence of order $\alpha \in (0,+\infty) \backslash \{1\}$ between $\kappa$ and $\eta$ conditionally to $\mu$ is \begin{align*} \He_\alpha(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu) = D_{f_\alpha}(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu) \: , \end{align*} for $f_\alpha : x \mapsto \frac{x^{\alpha} - 1}{\alpha - 1}$.
nodes.label: def:condHellingerAlpha

nodes.name: Data-processing inequality for Hellinger divergences
nodes.statement:
Let $\alpha > 0$, $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\kappa : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be a Markov kernel. Then $\He_\alpha(\kappa \circ \mu, \kappa \circ 
u) \le \He_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\alpha > 0$, $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be a Markov kernel.
nodes.label: thm:hellingerAlpha_data_proc

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:fDiv_data_proc_2}.
nodes.statement_short: Special case of the DPI for f-divergences.

nodes.name: Hellinger divergences are nonnegative
nodes.statement: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures. Then $\He_\alpha(\mu, \nu) \ge 0$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures.
nodes.label: lem:hellingerAlpha_nonneg

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_nonneg}.
nodes.statement_short: Nonnegativity of f-divergences.

nodes.name: Convexity of Hellinger divergences
nodes.statement: $(\mu, \nu) \mapsto \He_\alpha(\mu, \nu)$ is convex.
nodes.label: lem:hellingerAlpha_convex

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:fDiv_convex}
nodes.statement_short: Special case of joint convexity of f-divergences.

nodes.name: Rényi divergence
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$. The Rényi divergence of order $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ between $\mu$ and $
u$ is  egin{align*} R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \left\{  egin{array}{ll} - \log \left( 
u\{x \mid  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) > 0\} / 
u(\mathcal X) ight) & 	ext{for } \alpha = 0 \ \KL(\mu / \mu(\mathcal X), 
u / 
u(\mathcal X)) & 	ext{for } \alpha = 1 \  rac{1}{\alpha - 1} \log \left(  rac{(1 - \alpha) 
u(\mathcal X) + \alpha \mu(\mathcal X) + (\alpha - 1) \He_\alpha(\mu, 
u)}{\mu(\mathcal X)^\alpha 
u(\mathcal X)^{1 - \alpha}} ight) & 	ext{for } \alpha 
otin \{0, 1\} \end{array}ight. \end{align*} It is the Rényi divergence of the normalized measures $\mu / \mu(\mathcal X)$ and $
u / 
u(\mathcal X)$. For $\alpha 
otin \{0, 1\}$, the numerator inside the logarithm is $\int \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}ight)^\alpha d
u$.
nodes.label: def:Renyi

nodes.name: Rényi divergence of order 0
nodes.statement:
For $\mu$ a sigma-finite measure and $
u$ a finite measure \[R_0(\mu, 
u) = - \log(
u\{x \mid  rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x) > 0\}) \: .\]
assumptions: For $\mu$ a sigma-finite measure and $\nu$ a finite measure
nodes.label: lem:renyiDiv_zero

nodes.name: Rényi divergence is infinite iff mutually singular (order below 1)
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha \in [0, 1)$ and finite measures $\mu, 
u$, \[R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \infty \iff \mu \perp 
u \: .\]
assumptions: For $\alpha \in [0, 1)$ and finite measures $\mu, \nu$
nodes.label: lem:renyiDiv_eq_top_iff_mutuallySingular_of_lt_one

nodes.name: Rényi divergence as log-integral
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha \in (0,1)\cup(1, \infty)$ and finite measures $\mu, 
u$, if $\left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}ight)^\alpha$ is integrable with respect to $
u$ and $\mu \ll 
u$ then  egin{align*} R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) =  rac{1}{\alpha - 1} \log \int_x \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)^\alpha \partial 
u \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\alpha \in (0,1)\cup(1, \infty)$ and finite measures $\mu, \nu$

if $\left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}ight)^\alpha$ is integrable with respect to $
u$ and $\mu \ll 
u$
nodes.label: lem:renyi_eq_log_integral

nodes.name: Rényi divergence as log-integral under mu
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha \in (0,1)\cup(1, \infty)$ and finite measures $\mu, 
u$, if $\left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}ight)^\alpha$ is integrable with respect to $
u$ and $\mu \ll 
u$ then  egin{align*} R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) =  rac{1}{\alpha - 1} \log \int_x \left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}(x)ight)^{\alpha - 1} \partial \mu \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\alpha \in (0,1)\cup(1, \infty)$ and finite measures $\mu, \nu$

if $\left( rac{d \mu}{d 
u}ight)^\alpha$ is integrable with respect to $
u$ and $\mu \ll 
u$
nodes.label: lem:renyi_eq_log_integral'

nodes.name: Skew symmetry of Rényi divergences
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and finite measures $\mu, 
u$ with $\mu(\mathcal X) = 
u(\mathcal X)$, \[(1 - \alpha) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \alpha R_{1 - \alpha}(
u, \mu) \: .\]
assumptions: For $\alpha \in (0, 1)$ and finite measures $\mu, \nu$ with $\mu(\mathcal X) = \nu(\mathcal X)$
nodes.label: lem:renyi_symm

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Use Lemma~\ref{lem:hellingerAlpha_symm}.
nodes.statement_short: From the skew symmetry of Hellinger divergences.

nodes.name: Rényi divergence as cumulant generating function under nu
nodes.statement:
The cumulant generating function of $\log rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ under $
u$ is $\alpha \mapsto (\alpha - 1) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$.
conclusions:
The cumulant generating function of $\log rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ under $
u$ is $\alpha \mapsto (\alpha - 1) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_cgf

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Unfold the definitions, using Lemma~\ref{lem:renyi_eq_log_integral} for the Rényi divergence.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold definitions with the log-integral formula.

nodes.name: Rényi divergence as cumulant generating function under mu
nodes.statement:
Set $\alpha > 0$. If $R_{1+\alpha}(\mu, 
u) < \infty$, the cumulant generating function of $\log rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ under $\mu$ has value $\alpha R_{1+\alpha}(\mu, 
u)$ at $\alpha$.
assumptions: Set $\alpha > 0$.
If $R_{1+\alpha}(\mu, \nu) < \infty$
conclusions: the cumulant generating function of $\log\frac{d\mu}{d\nu}$ under $\mu$ has value $\alpha R_{1+\alpha}(\mu, \nu)$ at $\alpha$
nodes.label: lem:renyi_cgf_2

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Unfold the definitions, using Lemma~\ref{lem:renyi_eq_log_integral'} for the Rényi divergence.
nodes.statement_short: Unfold definitions with the log-integral formula under $\mu$.

nodes.name: Conditional Rényi divergence
nodes.statement: Let $\mu$ be a measure on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be two kernels. The conditional Rényi divergence of order $\alpha \in (0,+\infty) \backslash \{1\}$ between $\kappa$ and $\eta$ conditionally to $\mu$ is \begin{align*} R_\alpha(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu) =\frac{1}{\alpha - 1} \log (1 + (\alpha - 1) \He_\alpha(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu)) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:condRenyi

nodes.name: Data-processing inequality for Rényi divergences
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\kappa : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be a Markov kernel. Then $R_\alpha(\kappa \circ \mu, \kappa \circ 
u) \le R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be a Markov kernel.
nodes.label: thm:renyi_data_proc

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The function $x \mapsto \frac{1}{\alpha - 1}\log (1 + (\alpha - 1)x)$ is non-decreasing and $D_f$ satisfies the DPI (Theorem~\ref{thm:fDiv_data_proc_2}), hence we get the DPI for $R_\alpha$.
nodes.statement_short: Rényi is a non-decreasing transform of a Hellinger f-divergence, which satisfies the DPI.

nodes.name: Rényi data-processing for events
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $E$ be an event. Let $\mu_E$ and $
u_E$ be the two Bernoulli distributions with respective means $\mu(E)$ and $
u(E)$. Then $R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) \ge R_\alpha(\mu_E, 
u_E)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $E$ be an event.
Let $\mu_E$ and $\nu_E$ be the two Bernoulli distributions with respective means $\mu(E)$ and $\nu(E)$.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_data_proc_event

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
By Corollary~ef{cor:data_proc_event}, $D_f(\mu, 
u) \ge D_f(\mu_E, 
u_E)$, hence $R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) \ge R_\alpha(\mu_E, 
u_E)$.
nodes.statement_short: Event DPI for the underlying f-divergence, then monotone transform.

nodes.name: Rényi divergence continuous at order 0
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures. $R_0(\mu, 
u) = \lim_{\alpha \downarrow 0} R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_tendsto_renyi_zero

nodes.name: Rényi divergence left-continuous at order 1
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures. $R_1(\mu, 
u) = \lim_{\alpha \uparrow 1} R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_tendsto_renyi_one

nodes.name: Rényi divergence right-continuous at order 1
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures such that there exists $\alpha > 1$ with $R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$ finite. Then $R_1(\mu, 
u) = \lim_{\alpha \downarrow 1} R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures such that there exists $\alpha > 1$ with $R_\alpha(\mu, \nu)$ finite.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_tendsto_renyi_one_above

nodes.name: Rényi divergence is nondecreasing in the order
nodes.statement: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures. Then $\alpha \mapsto R_\alpha(\mu, \nu)$ is nondecreasing on $[0, + \infty)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_monotone

nodes.name: Continuity of Rényi divergence in the order
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures. Then $\alpha \mapsto R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$ is continuous on $[0, 1]$ and on $[0, \sup \{\alpha \mid R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) < \infty\})$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures.
conclusions: Then $\alpha \mapsto R_\alpha(\mu, \nu)$ is continuous on $[0, 1]$ and on $[0, \sup \{\alpha \mid R_\alpha(\mu, \nu) < \infty\})$.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_continuous

nodes.name: Tilted measure
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\alpha \in (0, +\infty)  ackslash \{1\}$. Let $p =  rac{d \mu}{d (\mu + 
u)}$ and $q =  rac{d 
u}{d (\mu + 
u)}$. We define a measure $\mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}$, absolutely continuous with respect to $\mu + 
u$ with density  egin{align*}  rac{d \mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}}{d (\mu + 
u)} = p^\alpha q^{1 - \alpha} e^{-(\alpha - 1)R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:renyiMeasure

nodes.name: Tilted measure absolute continuity
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha \in (0,1)$, $\mu^{(\alpha, 
u)} \ll \mu$ and $\mu^{(\alpha, 
u)} \ll 
u$.
assumptions: For $\alpha \in (0,1)$
nodes.label: lem:renyiMeasure_ac

nodes.name: Radon-Nikodym derivatives of the tilted measure
nodes.statement:
$ rac{d \mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}}{d 
u} = \left( rac{d\mu}{d
u}ight)^\alpha e^{-(\alpha - 1) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)}$~, $
u$-a.e., and $ rac{d \mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}}{d \mu} = \left( rac{d
u}{d\mu}ight)^{1 - \alpha} e^{-(\alpha - 1) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)}$~, $\mu$-a.e..
nodes.label: lem:rnDeriv_renyiMeasure

nodes.name: KL to the tilted measure
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u, \xi$ be three measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$. Then  egin{align*} \KL(\xi, \mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}) = \alpha \KL(\xi, \mu) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(\xi, 
u) - (1 - \alpha) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu, \xi$ be three measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$.
nodes.label: lem:kl_renyiMeasure_eq

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Unfold definitions and compute?
nodes.statement_short: Unfold definitions and compute.

nodes.name: Rényi divergence via KL to the tilted measure
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u, \xi$ be three measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$. Then  egin{align*} (1 - \alpha) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \alpha \KL(\mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}, \mu) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(\mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}, 
u) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu, \xi$ be three measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$.
nodes.label: cor:renyi_eq_add_kl

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:kl_renyiMeasure_eq} to $\xi = \mu^{(\alpha, \nu)}$.
nodes.statement_short: Take $\xi$ equal to the tilted measure in the KL identity.

nodes.name: Variational formula for Rényi divergences
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$. Then  egin{align*} (1 - \alpha) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)}\left( \alpha \KL(\xi, \mu) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(\xi, 
u) ight) \: . \end{align*} The infimum is attained at $\xi = \mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_eq_inf_add_kl

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~ef{lem:kl_renyiMeasure_eq} and Lemma~ef{lem:kl_nonneg}, for all $\xi$,  egin{align*} \alpha \KL(\xi, \mu) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(\xi, 
u) - (1 - \alpha) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \KL(\xi, \mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}) \ge 0 \: . \end{align*} We have then $(1 - \alpha) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) \le \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)}\left( \alpha \KL(\xi, \mu) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(\xi, 
u) ight)$. Corollary~ef{cor:renyi_eq_add_kl} proves the other inequality.
nodes.statement_short: KL identity with the tilted measure plus nonnegativity of KL gives one inequality; the tilted measure attains it.

nodes.name: Lower bound for every $\xi$ via the tilted measure identity
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~ef{lem:kl_renyiMeasure_eq} and Lemma~ef{lem:kl_nonneg}, for all $\xi$,  egin{align*} \alpha \KL(\xi, \mu) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(\xi, 
u) - (1 - \alpha) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \KL(\xi, \mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}) \ge 0 \: . \end{align*} We have then $(1 - \alpha) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) \le \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)}\left( \alpha \KL(\xi, \mu) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(\xi, 
u) ight)$.
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound for every $\xi$ via the tilted measure identity.

nodes.name: The tilted measure attains the bound
nodes.statement: Corollary~\ref{cor:renyi_eq_add_kl} proves the other inequality.
nodes.statement_short: The tilted measure attains the bound.

nodes.name: Rényi divergence as infimum of KL to products
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$. Let $\pi_\alpha = (\alpha, 1 - \alpha) \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and let $P : \{0,1\} ightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel with $P(0) = \mu$ and $P(1) = 
u$. Then  egin{align*} (1 - \alpha) R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)} \KL\left( \pi_\alpha 	imes \xi, \pi_\alpha \otimes P ight) \: . \end{align*} The infimum is attained at $\xi = \mu^{(\alpha, 
u)}$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$.
Let $\pi_\alpha = (\alpha, 1 - \alpha) \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and let $P : \{0,1\} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel with $P(0) = \mu$ and $P(1) = \nu$.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_eq_inf_kl

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} \KL\left( \pi_\alpha \times \xi, \pi_\alpha \otimes P \right) &= \alpha \KL(\xi, \mu) + (1 - \alpha) \KL(\xi, \nu) \: . \end{align*} The result is a rephrasing of Lemma~\ref{lem:renyi_eq_inf_add_kl}.
nodes.statement_short: Expand the KL of the joint laws and rephrase the variational formula.

nodes.name: Chain rule for Rényi divergences
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be two Markov kernels. Then $R_\alpha(\mu \otimes \kappa, 
u \otimes \eta) = R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) + R_\alpha(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu^{(\alpha, 
u)})$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ be two Markov kernels.
nodes.label: thm:renyi_chain_rule

nodes.name: Chain rule for Rényi divergences, with Bayesian inverse
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X ightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ two Markov kernels with Bayesian inverses $\kappa_\mu^\dagger$ and $\eta_
u^\dagger$. Then  egin{align*} R_\alpha(\mu \otimes \kappa, 
u \otimes \eta) = R_\alpha(\kappa \circ \mu, \eta \circ 
u) + R_\alpha(\kappa_\mu^\dagger, \eta_
u^\dagger \mid (\kappa \circ \mu)^{(\alpha, \eta \circ 
u)}) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two finite measures on $\mathcal X$ and $\kappa, \eta : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ two Markov kernels with Bayesian inverses $\kappa_\mu^\dagger$ and $\eta_\nu^\dagger$.
nodes.label: thm:renyi_compProd_bayesInv

nodes.name: Rényi divergence of products
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and $\xi, \lambda \in \mathcal P(\mathcal Y)$. Then $R_\alpha(\mu 	imes \xi, 
u 	imes \lambda) = R_\alpha(\mu, 
u) + R_\alpha(\xi, \lambda)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and $\xi, \lambda \in \mathcal P(\mathcal Y)$.
nodes.label: cor:renyi_prod_two

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:renyi_chain_rule} (the product of measures is a special case of $\otimes$). TODO: more details.
nodes.statement_short: Products are composition-products with constant kernels; apply the chain rule.

nodes.name: Tensorization of Rényi divergences, finite product
nodes.statement:
Let $I$ be a finite index set. Let $(\mu_i)_{i \in I}, (
u_i)_{i \in I}$ be probability measures on measurable spaces $(\mathcal X_i)_{i \in I}$. Then $R_\alpha (\prod_{i \in I} \mu_i, \prod_{i \in I} 
u_i) = \sum_{i \in I} R_\alpha(\mu_i, 
u_i)$.
assumptions: Let $I$ be a finite index set.
Let $(\mu_i)_{i \in I}, (\nu_i)_{i \in I}$ be probability measures on measurable spaces $(\mathcal X_i)_{i \in I}$.
nodes.label: thm:renyi_prod

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Induction over the finite index set, using Corollary~\ref{cor:renyi_prod_two}.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on the index set using the two-factor product formula.

nodes.name: Rényi divergence of i.i.d. products
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures on $\mathcal X$. Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and write $\mu^{\otimes n}$ for the product measure on $\mathcal X^n$ of $n$ times $\mu$. Then $R_\alpha(\mu^{\otimes n}, 
u^{\otimes n}) = n R_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures on $\mathcal X$.
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and write $\mu^{\otimes n}$ for the product measure on $\mathcal X^n$ of $n$ times $\mu$.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_prod_n

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:renyi_prod}.
nodes.statement_short: Special case of tensorization.

nodes.name: Tensorization of Rényi divergences, countable product
nodes.statement:
Let $I$ be a countable index set. Let $(\mu_i)_{i \in I}, (
u_i)_{i \in I}$ be probability measures on measurable spaces $(\mathcal X_i)_{i \in I}$. Then $R_\alpha (\prod_{i \in I} \mu_i, \prod_{i \in I} 
u_i) = \sum_{i \in I} R_\alpha(\mu_i, 
u_i)$.
assumptions: Let $I$ be a countable index set.
Let $(\mu_i)_{i \in I}, (\nu_i)_{i \in I}$ be probability measures on measurable spaces $(\mathcal X_i)_{i \in I}$.
nodes.label: thm:renyi_prod_countable

nodes.name: Squared Hellinger distance
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two measures. The squared Hellinger distance between $\mu$ and $
u$ is  egin{align*} \Hsq(\mu, 
u) = D_f(\mu, 
u) \quad 	ext{with } f: x \mapsto  rac{1}{2}\left( 1 - \sqrt{x} ight)^2 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:Hellinger

nodes.name: Hellinger and Rényi
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures. Then $R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u) = -2\log(1 - \Hsq(\mu, 
u))$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures.
nodes.label: lem:renyi_half_eq_log_hellinger

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
$R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u) = -2 \log (1 -  rac{1}{2} D_f(
u, \mu))$ for $f : x \mapsto -2 (\sqrt{x} - 1)$. Using Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_mul}, $R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u) = -2 \log (1 - D_g(
u, \mu))$ for $g(x) = 1 - \sqrt{x}$. It suffices then to show that $\Hsq(\mu, 
u) = D_g(\mu, 
u)$, which is true by an application of Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_add_linear}.
nodes.statement_short: Write $R_{1/2}$ via an f-divergence, rescale, and add a linear term to match the Hellinger function.

nodes.name: Express $R_{1/2}$ through an f-divergence and rescale
nodes.statement:
$R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u) = -2 \log (1 -  rac{1}{2} D_f(
u, \mu))$ for $f : x \mapsto -2 (\sqrt{x} - 1)$. Using Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_mul}, $R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u) = -2 \log (1 - D_g(
u, \mu))$ for $g(x) = 1 - \sqrt{x}$.
nodes.statement_short: Express $R_{1/2}$ through an f-divergence and rescale.

nodes.name: Match with the Hellinger function up to a linear term
nodes.statement: It suffices then to show that $\Hsq(\mu, \nu) = D_g(\mu, \nu)$, which is true by an application of Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_add_linear}.
nodes.statement_short: Match with the Hellinger function up to a linear term.

nodes.name: Squared Hellinger bounded by Rényi of order 1/2
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures. Then $2 \Hsq(\mu, 
u) \le R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures.
nodes.label: lem:hellinger_le_renyi

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Use Lemma~\ref{lem:renyi_half_eq_log_hellinger}, then $-\log(1 - x) \ge x$.
nodes.statement_short: From the exact relation and $-\log(1-x) \ge x$.

nodes.name: Squared Hellinger bounded by TV
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures. Then $\Hsq(\mu, 
u) \le \TV(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures.
nodes.label: lem:hellinger_le_tv

nodes.name: TV bounded by Hellinger
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures. Then $\TV(\mu, 
u) \le \sqrt{\Hsq(\mu, 
u)(2 - \Hsq(\mu, 
u))}$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures.
nodes.label: lem:tv_le_hellinger

nodes.name: Hellinger-TV comparison (quadratic form)
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures. Then  egin{align*}  rac{1}{2}(1 - \Hsq(\mu, 
u))^2 \le 1 - \TV(\mu, 
u) -  rac{1}{2}(1 - \TV(\mu, 
u))^2 \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures.
nodes.label: cor:one_sub_hellinger_squared_le_one_sub_tv

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
We use Lemma~ef{lem:tv_le_hellinger}.  egin{align*} 1 - \TV(\mu, 
u) -  rac{1}{2}(1 - \Hsq(\mu, 
u))^2 &=  rac{1}{2} - \TV(\mu, 
u) +  rac{1}{2}(\Hsq(\mu, 
u)(2 - \Hsq(\mu, 
u))) \ &\ge  rac{1}{2} - \TV(\mu, 
u) +  rac{1}{2}\TV^2(\mu, 
u) \ &=  rac{1}{2}(1 - \TV(\mu, 
u))^2 \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Rearrange and use TV bounded by Hellinger.

nodes.name: Two-sided Hellinger-TV comparison
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures. Then  egin{align*} 1 - \sqrt{1 - (1 - \Hsq(\mu, 
u))^2} \le 1 - \TV(\mu, 
u) \le 1 - \Hsq(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures.
nodes.label: cor:one_sub_hellinger_le_one_sub_tv

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Use Lemma~\ref{lem:tv_le_hellinger} and~\ref{lem:hellinger_le_tv}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the two Hellinger-TV inequalities.

nodes.name: TV of i.i.d. products bounded via Rényi of order 1/2
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\mu^{\otimes n}, 
u^{\otimes n}$ be their product measures on $\mathcal X^n$. Then  egin{align*}  rac{1}{2}e^{-n R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u)} \le 1 - \sqrt{1 - e^{-n R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u)}} \le 1 - \TV(\mu^{\otimes n}, 
u^{\otimes n}) \le e^{- rac{1}{2} n R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u)} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided exponential bounds on $1-\TV$ between $n$-fold products in terms of $nR_{1/2}$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures on $\mathcal X$ and let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, and $\mu^{\otimes n}, \nu^{\otimes n}$ be their product measures on $\mathcal X^n$.
nodes.label: cor:one_sub_tv_bound_renyi

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
Use Corollary~ef{cor:one_sub_hellinger_le_one_sub_tv} and Lemma~ef{lem:renyi_half_eq_log_hellinger} to get to a comparison of $\TV(\mu, 
u)$ and $R_{1/2}(\mu^{\otimes n}, 
u^{\otimes n})$. Finally $R_{1/2}(\mu^{\otimes n}, 
u^{\otimes n}) = n R_{1/2}(\mu, 
u)$ by Lemma~ef{lem:renyi_prod_n}.
nodes.statement_short: Hellinger-TV comparison, Hellinger-Rényi relation and tensorization of $R_{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Chernoff divergence
nodes.statement:
The Chernoff divergence of order $\alpha > 0$ between two measures $\mu$ and $
u$ on $\mathcal X$ is  egin{align*} C_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)}\max\{R_\alpha(\xi, \mu), R_\alpha(\xi, 
u)\} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:Chernoff

nodes.name: Chernoff information C
nodes.statement: Note: the name Chernoff divergence is usually reserved for $C_1$, and any reference to $C$ without subscript in this document refers to $C_1$.

nodes.name: Chernoff divergence of order 1 via KL
nodes.statement: $C_1(\mu, \nu) = \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)}\max\{\KL(\xi, \mu), \KL(\xi, \nu)\}$ .
nodes.label: lem:chernoff_eq_kl

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: This is $R_1 = \KL$ (by definition).
nodes.statement_short: $R_1 = \KL$ by definition.

nodes.name: Symmetry of the Chernoff divergence
nodes.statement: $C_\alpha(\mu, \nu) = C_\alpha(\nu, \mu)$.
nodes.label: lem:chernoff_symm

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Immediate from the definition.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the definition.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of the Chernoff divergence in the order
nodes.statement: The function $\alpha \mapsto C_\alpha(\mu, \nu)$ is monotone.
nodes.label: lem:chernoff_mono

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Consequence of Lemma~\ref{lem:renyi_monotone}.
nodes.statement_short: Consequence of monotonicity of Rényi divergences in the order.

nodes.name: Chernoff information as maximum of skewed Rényi divergences
nodes.statement: \begin{align*} C_1(\mu, \nu) = \max_{\alpha\in [0,1]} (1 - \alpha)R_\alpha(\mu, \nu) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: lem:chernoff_eq_max_renyi

nodes.name: Jensen-Shannon divergence
nodes.statement:
The Jensen-Shannon divergence indexed by $\alpha \in (0,1)$ between two measures $\mu$ and $
u$ is  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \alpha \KL(\mu, \alpha \mu + (1 - \alpha)
u) + (1 - \alpha) \KL(
u, \alpha \mu + (1 - \alpha)
u) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:jensenShannon

nodes.name: Jensen-Shannon divergence as KL of joint and product laws
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$. Let $\pi_\alpha = (\alpha, 1 - \alpha) \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and let $P : \{0,1\} ightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel with $P(0) = \mu$ and $P(1) = 
u$. Then  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \KL(\pi_\alpha \otimes P, \pi_\alpha 	imes (P \circ \pi_\alpha)) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$.
Let $\pi_\alpha = (\alpha, 1 - \alpha) \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and let $P : \{0,1\} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel with $P(0) = \mu$ and $P(1) = \nu$.
nodes.label: lem:jensenShannon_eq_kl

nodes.name: Jensen-Shannon divergence is an f-divergence
nodes.statement: $\JS_\alpha$ is an $f$-divergence for $f(x) = \alpha x \log(x) - (\alpha x + 1 - \alpha) \log (\alpha x + 1 - \alpha)$~.
conclusions: $\JS_\alpha$ is an $f$-divergence for $f(x) = \alpha x \log(x) - (\alpha x + 1 - \alpha) \log (\alpha x + 1 - \alpha)$
nodes.label: lem:jensenShannon_eq_fDiv

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
$(\mu, 
u) \mapsto \KL(\mu, \alpha \mu + (1 - \alpha) 
u)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto x\log\left( rac{x}{\alpha x + 1 - \alpha}ight)$ (Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_add_smul_right}). $(\mu, 
u) \mapsto \KL(
u, \alpha \mu + (1 - \alpha) 
u)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto x\log\left( rac{1}{\alpha x + 1 - \alpha}ight)$ (Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_add_smul_right'}). By Lemmas~ef{lem:fDiv_mul} and ef{lem:fDiv_add}, we obtain the result.
nodes.statement_short: Each KL term is an f-divergence by the mixture lemmas; combine by linearity in $f$.

nodes.name: First KL term is an f-divergence
nodes.statement: $(\mu, \nu) \mapsto \KL(\mu, \alpha \mu + (1 - \alpha) \nu)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto x\log\left(\frac{x}{\alpha x + 1 - \alpha}\right)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_add_smul_right}).
nodes.statement_short: First KL term is an f-divergence.

nodes.name: Second KL term is an f-divergence
nodes.statement:
$(\mu, 
u) \mapsto \KL(
u, \alpha \mu + (1 - \alpha) 
u)$ is an $f$-divergence for the function $x \mapsto x\log\left( rac{1}{\alpha x + 1 - \alpha}ight)$ (Lemma~ef{lem:fDiv_add_smul_right'}).
nodes.statement_short: Second KL term is an f-divergence.

nodes.name: Combine by linearity in $f$
nodes.statement: By Lemmas~\ref{lem:fDiv_mul} and \ref{lem:fDiv_add}, we obtain the result.
nodes.statement_short: Combine by linearity in $f$.

nodes.name: Symmetry of the Jensen-Shannon divergence
nodes.statement:
For $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$,  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \JS_{1 - \alpha}(
u, \mu) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\alpha \in (0,1)$ and $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$
nodes.label: lem:jensenShannon_symm

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Immediate from the definition.
nodes.statement_short: Immediate from the definition.

nodes.name: Variational formula for the Jensen-Shannon divergence
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$. Then  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)}\left( \alpha \KL(\mu, \xi) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(
u, \xi) ight) \: . \end{align*} The infimum is attained at $\xi = \alpha \mu + (1 - \alpha) 
u$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$.
nodes.label: lem:jensenShannon_eq_inf_add_kl

nodes.name: Jensen-Shannon divergence as infimum of KL to products
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$. Let $\pi_\alpha = (\alpha, 1 - \alpha) \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and let $P : \{0,1\} ightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel with $P(0) = \mu$ and $P(1) = 
u$. Then  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) = \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)} \KL\left( \pi_\alpha \otimes P, \pi_\alpha 	imes \xi ight) \: . \end{align*} The infimum is attained at $\xi = \alpha \mu + (1 - \alpha) 
u$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$.
Let $\pi_\alpha = (\alpha, 1 - \alpha) \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and let $P : \{0,1\} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel with $P(0) = \mu$ and $P(1) = \nu$.
nodes.label: lem:jensenShannon_eq_inf_kl

nodes.name: Subadditivity of Jensen-Shannon for i.i.d. products
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u$ be two probability measures on $\mathcal X$. Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and write $\mu^{\otimes n}$ for the product measure on $\mathcal X^n$ of $n$ times $\mu$. Then $\JS_\alpha(\mu^{\otimes n}, 
u^{\otimes n}) \le n \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u)$.
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu$ be two probability measures on $\mathcal X$.
Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and write $\mu^{\otimes n}$ for the product measure on $\mathcal X^n$ of $n$ times $\mu$.
nodes.label: lem:jensenShannon_prod_n

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~ef{lem:jensenShannon_eq_inf_add_kl},  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu^{\otimes n}, 
u^{\otimes n}) &= \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X^n)}\left( \alpha \KL(\mu^{\otimes n}, \xi) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(
u^{\otimes n}, \xi) ight) \ &\le \inf_{\zeta \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)}\left( \alpha \KL(\mu^{\otimes n}, \zeta^{\otimes n}) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(
u^{\otimes n}, \zeta^{\otimes n}) ight) \ &= n \inf_{\zeta \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)}\left( \alpha \KL(\mu, \zeta) + (1 - \alpha)\KL(
u, \zeta) ight) \ &= n \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Variational formula, restricted to product measures, then KL tensorization.

nodes.name: Jensen-Shannon bounded by Hellinger divergences
nodes.statement:
For $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and $\alpha, \lambda \in (0,1)$~,  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) \le  rac{(1 - \alpha)^{1 - \lambda} \alpha^\lambda}{\lambda^{1 - \lambda} (1 - \lambda)^\lambda} (1 - \lambda)\He_\lambda(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*} In particular,  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) &\le \left( rac{1 - \alpha}{\alpha}ight)^{1 - 2 \alpha} (1 - \alpha)\He_\alpha(\mu, 
u) \: , \ \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) &\le \alpha \He_{1 - \alpha}(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and $\alpha, \lambda \in (0,1)$
nodes.label: lem:jensenShannon_le_hellingerAlpha

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The main tool is Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_le_of_deriv2_le}. $\JS_\alpha$ is an $f$-divergence with function $f(x) = \alpha x \log(x) - (\alpha x + 1 - \alpha) \log (\alpha x + 1 - \alpha)$. On probability measures, $(1 - \lambda)\He_\lambda$ is an $f$-divergence with function $g(x) = 1 - x^\lambda + \lambda(x-1)$. These two functions satisfy $f(1) = 0$, $g(1) = 0$, $f'(1) = 0$, $g'(1) = 0$ and have second derivatives, hence Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_le_of_deriv2_le} applies and to obtain the inequality it suffices to compute $\sup_x\frac{f''(x)}{g''(x)}$~. \begin{align*} f''(x) &= \frac{\alpha(1 - \alpha)}{x(\alpha x + 1 - \alpha)} \: , \\ g''(x) &= \lambda (1 - \lambda) x^{\lambda - 2} \: . \end{align*} Let $h(x) = \frac{f''(x)}{g''(x)} = \frac{\alpha (1 - \alpha)}{\lambda (1 - \lambda)} \frac{x^{1 - \lambda}}{\alpha x + 1 - \alpha}$~. Its maximum is attained at a point where $h'(x) = 0$. \begin{align*} h'(x) = \frac{\alpha (1 - \alpha)}{\lambda (1 - \lambda)} \frac{(1 - \alpha)(1 - \lambda)x^{-\lambda} - \alpha \lambda x^{1 - \lambda}}{(\alpha x + 1 - \alpha)^2} \: . \end{align*} The optimum for $h$ is attained at $x = \frac{(1 - \alpha)(1 - \lambda)}{\alpha \lambda}$ and the maximal value of $h$ is $\frac{(1 - \alpha)^{1 - \lambda} \alpha^\lambda}{\lambda^{1 - \lambda} (1 - \lambda)^\lambda}$~.
nodes.statement_short: Compare second derivatives of the two generating functions and maximize their ratio.

nodes.name: Use the second-derivative comparison lemma
nodes.statement: The main tool is Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_le_of_deriv2_le}.
nodes.statement_short: Use the second-derivative comparison lemma.

nodes.name: Write both divergences as f-divergences
nodes.statement: $\JS_\alpha$ is an $f$-divergence with function $f(x) = \alpha x \log(x) - (\alpha x + 1 - \alpha) \log (\alpha x + 1 - \alpha)$. On probability measures, $(1 - \lambda)\He_\lambda$ is an $f$-divergence with function $g(x) = 1 - x^\lambda + \lambda(x-1)$.
nodes.statement_short: Write both divergences as f-divergences.

nodes.name: Check the hypotheses and reduce to bounding $f''/g''$
nodes.statement: These two functions satisfy $f(1) = 0$, $g(1) = 0$, $f'(1) = 0$, $g'(1) = 0$ and have second derivatives, hence Lemma~\ref{lem:fDiv_le_of_deriv2_le} applies and to obtain the inequality it suffices to compute $\sup_x\frac{f''(x)}{g''(x)}$~. \begin{align*} f''(x) &= \frac{\alpha(1 - \alpha)}{x(\alpha x + 1 - \alpha)} \: , \\ g''(x) &= \lambda (1 - \lambda) x^{\lambda - 2} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Check the hypotheses and reduce to bounding $f''/g''$.

nodes.name: Differentiate the ratio $h$
nodes.statement: Let $h(x) = \frac{f''(x)}{g''(x)} = \frac{\alpha (1 - \alpha)}{\lambda (1 - \lambda)} \frac{x^{1 - \lambda}}{\alpha x + 1 - \alpha}$~. Its maximum is attained at a point where $h'(x) = 0$. \begin{align*} h'(x) = \frac{\alpha (1 - \alpha)}{\lambda (1 - \lambda)} \frac{(1 - \alpha)(1 - \lambda)x^{-\lambda} - \alpha \lambda x^{1 - \lambda}}{(\alpha x + 1 - \alpha)^2} \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the ratio $h$.

nodes.name: Maximum value of $h$
nodes.statement: The optimum for $h$ is attained at $x = \frac{(1 - \alpha)(1 - \lambda)}{\alpha \lambda}$ and the maximal value of $h$ is $\frac{(1 - \alpha)^{1 - \lambda} \alpha^\lambda}{\lambda^{1 - \lambda} (1 - \lambda)^\lambda}$~.
nodes.statement_short: Maximum value of $h$.

nodes.name: Jensen-Shannon bounded by Hellinger, small lambda
nodes.statement:
For $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and $\alpha \in (0,1)$, $\lambda \le 1/2$~,  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) &\le \alpha^{1 - \lambda} \He_{1 - \lambda}(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and $\alpha \in (0,1)$, $\lambda \le 1/2$
nodes.label: cor:jensenShannon_le_hellingerAlpha_of_le_half

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~ef{lem:jensenShannon_le_hellingerAlpha} for $\alpha$ and $1 - \lambda$,  egin{align*} \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) &\le  rac{(1 - \alpha)^{\lambda} \alpha^{1 - \lambda}}{\lambda^{1 - \lambda} (1 - \lambda)^\lambda} \lambda \He_{1 - \lambda}(\mu, 
u) \ &= \alpha^{1 - \lambda} (1 - \alpha)^\lambda \left( rac{\lambda}{1 - \lambda}ight)^\lambda \He_{1 - \lambda}(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*} To get the result, use $1 - \alpha \le 1$ and $ rac{\lambda}{1 - \lambda} \le 1$ since it is increasing in $\lambda$ with value 1 at $\lambda = 1/2$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the general bound at $1-\lambda$ and bound the constants by 1.

nodes.name: Mutual information
nodes.statement: The mutual information is, for $\rho \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y)$~, \begin{align*} I(\rho) = \KL(\rho, \rho_X \times \rho_Y) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:mutualInfo

nodes.name: Conditional mutual information
nodes.statement:
Let $\kappa : \mathcal Z ightsquigarrow \mathcal X 	imes \mathcal Y$. The conditional mutual information of $\kappa$ with respect to $
u \in \mathcal M(\mathcal Z)$ is  egin{align*} I(\kappa \mid 
u) = \KL(\kappa, \kappa_X 	imes \kappa_Y \mid 
u) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.label: def:condMutualInfo

nodes.name: Mutual information as conditional KL
nodes.statement: For $\mu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ and $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ a Markov kernel, \begin{align*} I(\mu \otimes \kappa) = KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, \mu \times (\kappa \circ \mu)) = KL(\kappa, \kappa \circ \mu \mid \mu) \: , \end{align*} where in the conditional divergence the measure $\kappa \circ \mu$ should be understood as the constant kernel from $\mathcal X$ to $\mathcal Y$ with that value.
assumptions: For $\mu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ and $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ a Markov kernel
nodes.label: lem:mutualInfo_eq_condKL

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: The first equality is the definition of $I$, together with $(\mu \otimes \kappa)_X = \mu$ (since $\kappa$ is Markov) and $(\mu \otimes \kappa)_Y = \kappa \circ \mu$. The second equality is from $KL(\kappa, \eta \mid \mu) = KL(\mu \otimes \kappa, \mu \otimes \eta)$. (TODO: now from a lemma, soon by definition).
nodes.statement_short: Marginals of $\mu\otimes\kappa$, then the composition-product form of conditional KL.

nodes.name: Symmetry of mutual information
nodes.statement: $I(\rho_\leftrightarrow) = I(\rho)$~.
nodes.label: lem:mutualInfo_symm

nodes.name: Mutual information equals Jensen-Shannon divergence
nodes.statement:
Let $\mu, 
u \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$. Let $\pi_\alpha = (\alpha, 1 - \alpha) \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and let $P : \{0,1\} ightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel with $P(0) = \mu$ and $P(1) = 
u$. Then  egin{align*} I(\pi_\alpha \otimes P) = \JS_\alpha(\mu, 
u) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: Let $\mu, \nu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and let $\alpha \in (0, 1)$.
Let $\pi_\alpha = (\alpha, 1 - \alpha) \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and let $P : \{0,1\} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal X$ be the kernel with $P(0) = \mu$ and $P(1) = \nu$.
nodes.label: lem:mutualInfo_eq_jensenShannon

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: Use Lemma~\ref{lem:mutualInfo_eq_condKL} and Lemma~\ref{lem:jensenShannon_eq_kl}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine the conditional-KL form of mutual information with the JS-KL identity.

nodes.name: Data-processing inequality for mutual information
nodes.statement: For $\rho \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y)$, $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal X'$ and $\eta : \mathcal Y \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y'$ two Markov kernels, \begin{align*} I((\kappa \parallel \eta) \circ \rho) \le I(\rho) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\rho \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X \times \mathcal Y)$, $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal X'$ and $\eta : \mathcal Y \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y'$ two Markov kernels
nodes.label: thm:mutualInfo_data_proc

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: $((\kappa \parallel \eta) \circ \rho)_{X'} = \kappa \circ \rho_X$ and $((\kappa \parallel \eta) \circ \rho)_{Y'} = \eta \circ \rho_Y$ hence \begin{align*} ((\kappa \parallel \eta) \circ \rho)_{X'} \times ((\kappa \parallel \eta) \circ \rho)_{Y'} &= (\kappa \circ \rho_X) \times (\eta \circ \rho_Y) = (\kappa \parallel \eta) \circ (\rho_X \times \rho_Y) \: . \end{align*} By the data-processing inequality for $\KL$ (Theorem~\ref{thm:kl_data_proc}), \begin{align*} I((\kappa \parallel \eta) \circ \rho) &= \KL((\kappa \parallel \eta) \circ \rho, (\kappa \parallel \eta) \circ (\rho_X \times \rho_Y)) \\ &\le \KL(\rho, \rho_X \times \rho_Y) \\ &= I(\rho) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Processing commutes with taking marginals; apply the DPI for KL.

nodes.name: Mutual information decreases along a Markov chain
nodes.statement: For $\mu \in \mathcal X$, $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ and $\eta : \mathcal Y \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Z$ two Markov kernels, \begin{align*} I(\mu \otimes (\eta \circ \kappa)) \le I(\mu \otimes \kappa) \: . \end{align*}
assumptions: For $\mu \in \mathcal X$, $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ and $\eta : \mathcal Y \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Z$ two Markov kernels
nodes.label: cor:mutualInfo_compProd_le

nodes.name: Mutual information data processing for a Markov chain
nodes.statement:
That corollary corresponds to the following situation: 3 random variables $X, Y, Z$ have the dependency structure $X \to Y \to Z$ and $\mu$ is the law of $X$, $\mu \otimes \kappa$ is the law of $(X, Y)$ and $\mu \otimes (\eta \circ \kappa)$ is the law of $(X, Z)$.
With the usual $I(X, Y)$ notation, the corollary statement is $I(X, Z) \le I(X, Y)$~.

nodes.name: Proof
nodes.statement: First, rewrite $\mu \otimes (\eta \circ \kappa) = (\mathrm{id} \parallel \eta) \circ (\mu \otimes \kappa)$. Then apply Theorem~\ref{thm:mutualInfo_data_proc}.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite as processing of the second coordinate and apply the DPI for mutual information.

nodes.name: Left D-mutual information
nodes.statement: Let $D$ be a divergence between measures. The left $D$-mutual information for a measure $\mu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ and a kernel $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ is \begin{align*} I_D^L(\mu, \kappa) = \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal Y)} D(\mu \times \xi, \mu \otimes \kappa) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3.2 New definitions related to the mutual information
nodes.label: def:mutualInfoLeft

nodes.name: Right D-mutual information
nodes.statement: Let $D$ be a divergence between measures. The right $D$-mutual information for a measure $\mu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$ and a kernel $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ is \begin{align*} I_D^R(\mu, \kappa) = \inf_{\xi \in \mathcal P(\mathcal Y)} D(\mu \otimes \kappa, \mu \times \xi) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3.2 New definitions related to the mutual information
nodes.label: def:mutualInfoRight

nodes.name: Left KL-mutual information equals skewed Rényi
nodes.statement: For $\mu \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and $\kappa : \{0,1\} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$, \begin{align*} I_{\KL}^L(\mu, \kappa) = (1 - \mu_0) R_{\mu_0}(\kappa_0, \kappa_1) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3.2 New definitions related to the mutual information
assumptions: For $\mu \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and $\kappa : \{0,1\} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$
nodes.label: lem:mutualInfoLeft_eq_renyi

nodes.name: Right KL-mutual information equals mutual information
nodes.statement: For $\mu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$, \begin{align*} I_{\KL}^R(\mu, \kappa) = I(\mu \otimes \kappa) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3.2 New definitions related to the mutual information
assumptions: For $\mu \in \mathcal P(\mathcal X)$ and $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$
nodes.label: lem:mutualInfoRight_eq_mutualInfo

nodes.name: Right KL-mutual information equals Jensen-Shannon
nodes.statement: For $\mu \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and $\kappa : \{0,1\} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$, \begin{align*} I_{\KL}^R(\mu, \kappa) = \JS_{\mu_0}(\kappa_0, \kappa_1) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3.2 New definitions related to the mutual information
assumptions: For $\mu \in \mathcal P(\{0,1\})$ and $\kappa : \{0,1\} \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$
nodes.label: cor:mutualInfoRight_eq_jensenShannon

nodes.name: Data-processing for left and right D-mutual information
nodes.statement: If the divergence $D$ satisfies the data-processing inequality, then for all $\mu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$, $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ and all Markov kernels $\eta : \mathcal Y \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Z$ then \begin{align*} I_D^L(\mu, \eta \circ \kappa) \le I_D^L(\mu, \kappa) \: , \\ I_D^R(\mu, \eta \circ \kappa) \le I_D^R(\mu, \kappa) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3.2 New definitions related to the mutual information
assumptions: If the divergence $D$ satisfies the data-processing inequality
for all $\mu \in \mathcal M(\mathcal X)$, $\kappa : \mathcal X \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Y$ and all Markov kernels $\eta : \mathcal Y \rightsquigarrow \mathcal Z$
nodes.label: thm:mutualInfoLeft_comp_le

nodes.name: D_f-mutual information lower bound on Bayes risks
nodes.statement: Let $\pi \in \mathcal P(\Theta)$ and $P : \Theta \rightsquigarrow \mathcal X$. Suppose that the loss $\ell'$ of an estimation task with kernel $P$ takes values in $[0,1]$. Then \begin{align*} I_{D_f}^L(\pi, P) &\ge d_f(\mathcal R_\pi^{d_\Theta}, \mathcal R_\pi^P) \: , \\ I_{D_f}^R(\pi, P) &\ge d_f(\mathcal R_\pi^P, \mathcal R_\pi^{d_\Theta}) \: . \end{align*}
nodes.section: 3.2 New definitions related to the mutual information
assumptions: Let $\pi \in \mathcal P(\Theta)$ and $P : \Theta \rightsquigarrow \mathcal X$.
Suppose that the loss $\ell'$ of an estimation task with kernel $P$ takes values in $[0,1]$.
nodes.label: lem:mutualInfoLeft_estimation_ge

nodes.name: Proof
